_field_contract: resume.sh does os.path.isdir(worktree) and git rev-list origin/<branch>..HEAD, so `worktree` and `branch` must each be ONE value. An agent working two repos records the other in second_worktree/second_branch, which resume.sh ignores. Writing 'a and b' there makes the next report say 'no worktree' for a worktree that is fine.

_findings.nft -c cannot run in a build container: netlink: Error: cache initialization failed: Operation not permitted. nft -c applies nothing, but libnftables opens a netlink socket and lists the LIVE ruleset before it will look at a file, and that needs CAP_NET_ADMIN over a real netns. The build had none, so the parser never ran and the step exited 1 at STEP 99/148. Fixed by giving it a netns of its own: unshare --user --map-root-user --net nft -c -f. Proved four ways with a fake unshare on PATH - parses / rejects a mutant at line 60 col 56-60 / unshare absent / unshare REFUSED - because the first draft classified unshare's own refusal as 'nft rejected the ruleset' and would have failed the build a second time on a false diagnosis.
_findings.tests/test-apex-firewall.sh had never on: Its parse case SKIPped for every non-root caller, so CI had never run it. Same private netns, same three-way verdict: 31 passed/1 skipped -> 32 passed/0 skipped, and against a mutant ruleset 30 passed/2 failed with the failure named.

_findings.the expiry test used an openssl flag the: apex-remote-core/tests/tls.rs minted its out-of-date certificate with openssl x509 -req -not_before/-not_after, which arrived in OpenSSL 3.5. This laptop has 3.5.7, ubuntu-latest has 3.0.13, where x509 answers 'Use -help for summary' and exits non-zero - a message nobody reads as a version problem. Replaced with openssl ca -startdate/-enddate and verified inside a docker.io/library/ubuntu:24.04 container with the runner's own openssl rather than by another 45-minute build. Fixed in 9f352724; the rust job is green on it.

_findings.root looked for every user's lid config: Merging the four rescued branches took the workspace to 588 passed / 1 failed, and the failure was a PRODUCT defect. owner_configs resolved another user's config path through the INVOKING process's XDG_CONFIG_HOME, so the uid scan - which is the path the root driver takes - looked for every user's lid config inside root's own XDG directory, and on any machine where that variable is set the owner's pin would have been ignored silently. It is also why the test passed alone and failed in a full run: a gaming.rs test sets XDG_CONFIG_HOME in the same process. Split into invoker_config_path and config_path_for_home; 2998 passed, 0 failed; restoring the single function reddens the test by name.
_findings.the image job died on a runner shutdown,: 34674350798: changes OK, rust OK, core OK, BASE OK in 14m - then image failed with 'The runner has received a shutdown signal' at 06:03, twelve minutes into the push step, with every build step green and no ::error:: emitted. Re-run with gh run rerun --failed rather than rebuilding core and base again.
_findings.errexit does not apply to a `!`-inverted: THE defect class of round 21, and it invalidated three of my own fixes from the same day. bash(1) under `set -e` exempts 'any command in a pipeline but the last, or if the command's return value is being inverted with !'. So `set -e; ! grep -q x <<<x; echo REACHED` prints REACHED. Every `! grep` in these Containerfiles is written as a build-time refusal and 46 of them failed nothing — they are mid-stanza, so their status is discarded and the build only ever stops if some LATER command in the same RUN fails. Found by the p1-063 lid agent in its own stanza; it wrote its refusals as `if ... exit 1` from the start and that is the idiom adopted. Ten of the 46 are not greps and were never in reach of the resolver at all: `apex-mux nonsense-verb`, `apex vm create --graphics spice`, `apex secret --help`, `apex recover reset` as root, `command -v qemu-system-x86_64` — all carrying real security decisions and asserting nothing. Fixed in b1d1c5bf; the gate now reports a fourth number and exits 1 on it.
_findings.706489ec misdiagnosed what broke the bui: 706489ec's message says a bare `! grep -q '_keep'` 'failed on a correct file, and `set -eux` made that a failed image build'. It CANNOT have. `git show 5cb71ea0` puts all three polkit refusals in ONE commit with `<allow_inactive>yes` last, so the `_keep` line was mid-stanza from birth and never ran an exit status anybody read. The five-day breakage was the EFFECTIVE assertions: the nft check and the ApexShellKeybinds grep (neither inverted) and `mouse = true` (last in its stanza). Reasoned, not reproduced, by an agent with the same blind spot. Worth keeping as the lesson: a diagnosis written from a plausible mechanism inherits that mechanism's assumptions.

_findings.the ten non-grep refusals were all TRUE,: Checked locally against a debug build and the shipped libexec scripts before the image could answer, because a build takes 45 minutes to reach them. All ten pass: `apex secret --help` exposes no value-returning verb; `apex vm create` refuses both secure-boot flags together (rc=2) and --graphics spice (rc=2); apex-aid --listen refuses with SO_PEERCRED named (rc=1); apex-vm doctor exits 1 and says both 'sudo apex install' and 'MISSING'; apex-mux, apex-agent-focus, apex-agent-review and apex-project-windows all refuse bad input; qemu and virsh are absent. So making them effective changes nothing about what passes — it changes what would be CAUGHT. Four are the build's to answer and were deliberately not faked here: `apex recover reset` as root, niri validate, the zellij layout, and plugin-verdict.js, which need the provisioned config or the vendored MJS.
_findings.`apex vm --help` wrote to stderr \u2014: usage() did `cat >&2`, and that function is reached ONLY by `""|-h|--help|help` (an unknown command goes to `die`), so it is always an explicit help request. Measured: 0 lines on stdout, 46 on stderr; now 46 and 0. It failed base at STEP 120 of 165 in run 34687788947 with NO FATAL printed, which is the tell that it was a plain assertion rather than one of the converted refusals. apex-mux has the same `cat >&2` and was deliberately LEFT ALONE: there `usage` IS the error path. Fixed in d12d3450.
_findings.the assertion checker was skipping pipe-: It matched greps against physical LINES. A grep at the tail of a pipe looked like a grep with no file and was skipped with `continue` — not checked, and not counted as unchecked either, which is how it reported '0 failed' for 50 minutes while `apex-vm --help | grep` could never pass. A grep whose pattern and path sit on two lines — how this file writes every long one — looked identical. It now resolves from the joined top-level segments it already computes for the inert check: 98 checked -> 106, and unresolved rose to 154 because silent skips are finally visible. Both detectors re-proved against mutants after the refactor.
_findings.apex-shell CI had never run green, and t: The `arch-validate` job runs in archlinux:latest. Its Internationalisation baseline step began `sudo apt-get update -qq` — the ONLY apt call in the workflow, every other install uses pacman — so the step died before tests/run-i18n-test.sh ever started and a 12-assertion suite had never run on a second machine. The `|| echo` fallback was on the install line, not the update line. Fixed in apex-shell cfda0ee. The earlier failure on the same run was two greps still spelling `Theme.` after P1-040 moved TopBar.qml to a per-output `theme` object (a2c66f2). Note for everyone: `gh workflow run ci.yml --repo AndreNijman/apex-shell --ref roadmap/v2.2` WORKS, contrary to ci.yml's own comment — a second machine for one command, no push, no PR.
_findings.\"there is no worktrees verb\" was read: p1-053a recorded, and I repeated into a dispatch brief and into P1-054's evidence, that apex-agent-core's Request has no worktrees/projects/profile verb. It had read apexd/apex-agent-core/src/request.rs, whose Request is a VALIDATION-ERROR enum (UnknownVerb, NoPackages, TooManyPackages, BadPackageName, BadReason, UnexpectedArguments). The WIRE protocol is apexd/apex-agent-core/src/protocol.rs: `pub enum Request` at line 531 has Worktrees at 723, and Response at 1138 has it at 1172. Full vocabulary, 28 verbs: Attach Decide DeclareOrigin ElevationChallenge Event Grants Hello Info Inject Input List Logs PrivilegeRequest Prune Remove RenewSystemGrant RequestExecuted Requests Resize Revoke RevokeSystemGrant Run SecretUse Signal SystemGrants Telemetry ToolCheck Worktrees. Round 3's worktrees request and parser were CORRECT and were deleted for a bad reason; p1-053b caught it and restored them. Profile and Projects ARE genuinely absent. P1-054's evidence now carries the correction. Lesson: grep the enum before repeating a 'verb X does not exist' claim.
_findings.the squash-merge comparison integrate-4: `git merge-tree --write-tree` never equals the tip's tree for these branches: they all append to .github/workflows/ci.yml, so it exits 1 with a CONFLICT there and the 'extra content' in the merged tree is conflict markers that read exactly like stranded work. followups-3 used the exact-content test in ROADMAP/state/unlanded.py::squashed_at instead. SEVEN remote branches were then deleted after content verification, with pre-deletion shas recorded and local worktrees still holding every one — orchestrator re-verified: the three apex-os refs are gone from origin and a887c5fd, aa7bf627 and 16fc8aeb are all still reachable locally, so the claim holds. task/p1-018-mcp-auth was the one that FAILED the content test and was deleted anyway for a stated reason: the tip SUPERSEDED its design (service.rs:1445 records that P1-018 gated --everywhere on OperationSpec::names_nothing, replaced later by same_everywhere).
_findings.the provenance flake was ETXTBSY, and it: I had guessed it was the same `set_var` shape as the agentd flake. It was not. followups-3 separated the guard from the reporting fix (they had landed in one commit, so nothing had ever distinguished 'the panic names ETXTBSY' from 'the retry stops it') and ran both builds through one harness: unguarded 40 failures / 1000 runs (4.0%), guarded 0 / 1200. _findings.the L16 boots an image older than the ve: Input (8c3958df) and Worktrees both landed 2026-09-08; the booted deployment was built 2026-09-05. So the worktrees and input happy paths CANNOT be exercised against this machine's daemon at all — a could-not-run, not a failure, and it will stay that way until an image build lands. _findings.the Android unit has been wrong about th: Once fatally — correct worktrees code was deleted over a claim read off a validation-error enum. p1-053b closed the class by construction rather than by care: android/core/src/test/resources/requests.json is every request the app builds, asserted by Kotlin against the builders AND by apexd/apex-agent-core/tests/android_requests_wire.rs against Request's own serde. A verb that does not exist now fails to deserialize instead of being argued about. Two real defects also fixed: connecting to a second machine kept the first one's worktrees, grants and pending approvals; and replyToSession reported every failure as 'may already have been delivered', the opposite of what protocol.rs guarantees — told it might have landed, a user does not resend and the agent waits forever.
_findings.a fail-open in the plugin policy, caught: Round 3 shipped `plugins` in AgentPolicy::dimensions() but NOT in the version table, and check_daemon_understands maps an unrecognised name onto POLICY_DIMENSIONS_VERSION. Config::policy copies the field straight through, so `plugins = "none"` in agent.toml reached that path WITH NO CLI FLAG AT ALL: the check passed, the daemon dropped the key, and the session loaded every plugin and ran every SessionStart hook. Fixed in 6d3ce356 — PROTOCOL_VERSION 7->8, PLUGIN_POLICY_VERSION = 8, and the table split out as settings_a_daemon_could_drop so it can be asserted without a socket. ORCHESTRATOR CHECKED THE BLAST RADIUS: the L16's shipped /usr/bin/apex has NO plugin policy at all (0 `--plugins` flags in help, 0 string matches in the binary) and there is no agent.toml on the machine, so the fail-open lived only in unreleased branch code and never reached Andre. The live daemon answers protocol 1 and refuses --plugins outright, which is fail-closed and correct.
_findings.--plugins has never gone through the dae: The L16's daemon answers protocol 1, so `apex agent run --plugins none` is refused with 'speaks protocol 1 and would ignore --plugins' and no session starts — correct behaviour, but it means session.rs -> document wiring is unit-tested only. Closing it needs a daemon built from the tip, i.e. restarting apex-agentd or an image. THAT IS ANDRE'S CALL, not an agent's, and the standing rule forbids `pkill apex-agentd`. Also: the live plugin-removal test is #[ignore]d and ran on the L16 only — CI installs no `claude`, so CI has never held that check; the suite prints a '----' could-not-run line counted separately from PASS rather than passing vacuously.

The worst instance: tests/test-apex-lid.sh, SIXTY assertions for P1-063 — the lid behaviour Andre asked for in his own words — had never been executed by any CI run. Also unrun: test-apex-firewall.sh, test-secret-at-rest.sh, test-apex-trust-enforcement.sh, test-apex-devices.sh, test-device-image.sh, test-device-services-netns.sh, test-apex-firewall-ssh.sh, test-apex-multilib.sh. It caught the orchestrator's own error on its first run: test-labwc-session.sh was wrongly listed as exempt.
_findings.102 of 140 shell scripts were never lint: pr-validation.yml lints a hand-written LIST. 140 shell scripts exist under tests/ and files/; 38 were named. Unlinted were four suites landed in the previous two days and both checkers written to catch this species of gap. tests/check-shellcheck-coverage.sh now discovers them. 78 of the 102 were already clean; the 28 that are not are on tests/shellcheck-known-failing.txt, generated from the gate's exact invocation. CHECKED, not assumed: none of the 28 is a live hazard — apex-shell-firstrun's four SC2088 are a `case` pattern matching a literal ~/ prefix and three human-readable messages, and the rest are SC2034/SC2155/SC2010/SC2148.
_findings.a negative control that could not fire,: Testing the new lint gate, the orchestrator probed with `rm -rf $x/tmp`. SC2086 is INFO-level and the gate runs `-S warning`, so the probe could never have triggered the condition — an assertion that cannot fail, written while building the tool that finds assertions that cannot fail. Caught by running it and seeing exit 0. Redone with SC2034. Recorded in the commit message rather than quietly corrected, and every agent brief now carries the rule: whenever you assert a check catches X, make X happen and watch it go red.
_findings.the SBOM step was short of TIME, not res: base passed for the first time since the seven can-only-fail fixes, then image died on 'syft did not finish cataloguing the image in 15 minutes'. The df/free numbers added in an earlier round are what make it a fact rather than a guess: 86 GB free, 14.8 GB available. The image is large (ChatGPT 1.3 GB + Claude Desktop 548 MB in core) and syft pulls the whole thing from the registry first. Restricting cataloguers to the RPM db was REJECTED: the Electron trees are where a CVE question lands, and an RPM-only SBOM answers with silence while looking authoritative. _findings.the suite gate read a COMMENT naming a s: Written by the orchestrator into the very tool built to find this class. The gate matched a basename anywhere under .github/workflows/, and its own step comment in pr-validation.yml names tests/test-apex-lid.sh while explaining the defect — so it reported the lid suite as run when nothing had wired it. Same shape as the forbid-check this repo once shipped that matched the comment explaining what it forbade. It did damage first: the false match fired the stale-exemption arm against test-labwc-session.sh, the orchestrator believed it and deleted that line, recording a never-run suite as covered. Lines whose first non-blank char is # are now stripped; counts corrected 59->57 run, 12->13 exempt. Both arms re-proved, arm A specifically against a comment-only mention.
_findings.nothing selected on .github/workflows \u: No selector mentioned workflow files, so a workflow-only change set rust/installer/engine/android all false, skipped every job and passed. The sharp version: deleting the line that invokes a suite IS a workflow-only change, so check-suites-run-in-ci.sh — the gate whose purpose is noticing an unrun suite — would have been disarmed by the very deletion it exists to catch. Added to the engine selector and proved end to end by deleting every test-apex-vm.sh invocation and watching it fail.

_ci: CI RAN FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THIS PROGRAM, and this is the record of what that cost and bought. pr-validation.yml triggered ONLY on `pull_request: branches: [main]`, and the program is forbidden from opening a PR until final integration - so sixty landed items, twelve landings and ~2000 Rust tests had been verified on exactly one laptop. `gh run list --branch roadmap/v2.2` returned nothing at all. Fixed in four commits, each one exposing the next problem: (1) push + workflow_dispatch triggers added; the first run failed in 18s. (2) The parity check cloned apex-shell's DEFAULT branch, so it compared apex-os roadmap/v2.2 against apex-shell main and reported drift on two touchpad defaults - while the two INTEGRATION branches agreed perfectly at 22 settings. It now clones the matching branch and PRINTS which one it used. THE DRIFT IT EXPOSED IS REAL AND IS KEPT: apex-shell main has drag_lock=true and click_method=clickfinger where apex-os main's generator has false and buttonAreas, so whoever does the final integration must land both sides together or opening the Input page silently changes a user's touchpad behaviour. (3) The path classifier read github.event.pull_request.* and died with exit 128 on a push; it is now event-aware and, when no range can be determined, selects EVERYTHING - this file already records four occasions where a selector picked nothing, the job skipped, and the workflow passed. (4) Six confinement assertions in mcp_sidecar_live.rs had never run anywhere but the L16 because the runner has no bubblewrap; installed rather than skipped, because they are the assertions that the sandbox IS a sandbox. Then bwrap failed on Ubuntu 24.04's kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1, so the sysctl is relaxed and PROVEN with a smoke check before any test runs. THE FINDING THAT PAYS FOR ALL OF IT: on the runner, /proc/N/cgroup reads '/system.slice/hosted-compute-agent.service', which is neither a login session nor a user service - a THIRD classification distinct from the L16's session scope and from scheduled-job. Two request_origin tests fail there while nine pass. Four rounds of orchestrators wrote that the workflow file was the only evidence of what CI presents; it is now measured, and p0-014 has been sent the exact string while it is still live.
